meta.product: MR conventional magnet line (1.5 tesla and 3 tesla scanners built around a helium-cooled superconducting magnet)
meta.tolerance_line: An install more than 30 days late, or a line stop longer than 30 days, goes past the 30-day limit.
meta.confidence_basis: All 11 panel members agreed on both questions and on which site or supplier fails in each future. The dates after 2028 are votes on undated events, and the numbers that decide whether a failure is real (days of helium on hand, weeks of logic stock and the cold-head parent's share of revenue) are Placeholders that no owner has confirmed. Every internal value in this run is synthetic.

risks.name: United States magnet plant
risks.sentence: One plant winds and tests every magnet for the Americas and Europe, and a storm, a strike or a grid curtailment stops it with nothing to cover.

risks.name: China plant
risks.sentence: One plant builds every magnet and system for Asia inside a counterparty's borders, and a listing or a trade rupture strands it.

risks.name: United States hub
risks.sentence: One site assembles every system for two regions, so any stop there delays every install at once.

risks.name: Superconducting wire
risks.sentence: Every conventional magnet is wound from one mill's superconducting wire, and qualifying a second mill takes longer than the backlog covers.

risks.name: Cold heads
risks.sentence: One maker in Japan supplies the cold heads that keep every magnet cold, and without one a magnet cannot ship or stay cold in the field.

risks.name: Programmable logic
risks.sentence: The control electronics for every system use programmable logic that a foundry interruption or an entity listing can stop.

risks.name: Technicians
risks.sentence: The winding and cryogenic trades at the United States plant live in one town, and a strike or a retirement cliff cuts output without any supplier failing.

risks.name: Helium cover
risks.sentence: Helium cover at the United States plant is shorter than the time to reroute a shipment, so any interruption to power, road or port reaches the line.

uncertainties.question: Will something outside the OEM stop a part or a shipping route for more than 30 days before 2031?
uncertainties.end_a: No. Every measure costs money but stays inside the 30-day limit. Tariffs, payment friction and customs time raise the bill without stopping anything for more than 30 days.
uncertainties.end_b: Yes. A producer country puts wire, niobium or cold heads under export control, an entity listing cuts the flow of parts through the China plant, or a sole supplier's owner leaves the MR business.
uncertainties.lean_sentence: The indicators lean weakly toward no. On 11 Oct 2026 the Section 232 investigation into medical products (a United States national-security trade investigation) had produced no proclamation, the trade truce with China was holding until its notice date, and no export-control listing named superconducting wire or cold heads.
uncertainties.settles_a: The answer settles as no if the 2027 sourcing cycle closes with the China truce renewed, the Section 232 report limited to finished scanners, and no export-control listing of wire, niobium or cold heads.
uncertainties.settles_b: The answer settles as yes if a notice in the Federal Register, from China's Ministry of Commerce or from a producer country names any of those parts, if an entity listing (the United States adding a company to its export blacklist) names the China plant or its logic supplier, or if a parent company announces the sale or closure of the wire mill or the cold-head plant.

uncertainties.question: In 2031, will helium supply still decide whether a magnet ships?
uncertainties.end_a: Yes. The Gulf route stays impaired or allocated, most new builds are still conventional, and a sealed magnet still needs a helium delivery for cool-down and testing.
uncertainties.end_b: No. Helium returns to a buyers' market, or sealed magnets take most new builds with a small test draw, so the cold head becomes the part that keeps every magnet cold.
uncertainties.lean_sentence: The indicators lean clearly toward yes. In the latest daily count, on 4 Oct 2026, four ships crossed the Gulf strait against a typical 85 (International Monetary Fund PortWatch data). Helium is bought on allocation letters, and no 3 tesla sealed magnet has been cleared for sale in the United States.
uncertainties.settles_a: The answer settles as yes if a United States helium allocation or export rule is proposed, if repairs to Qatar's damaged helium plant slip past 2028, or if a sealed magnet's test draw is confirmed as the size of a full helium delivery.
uncertainties.settles_b: The answer settles as no if the Gulf strait reopens to insured shipping and the allocation letters stop, if a 3 tesla sealed magnet is cleared, or if the test draw is confirmed as one gas cylinder rather than a full delivery.

futures.name: Trade costs rise and helium still limits shipments
futures.sentence: Trade rules raise costs but cut nothing off, and magnets still need helium to ship. Delivery dates depend on helium containers, the power grid and the roads rather than on trade rules.
futures.what_happens: The truce is renewed and no part is listed. The Gulf route stays near closed and both plants buy helium on allocation, the United States plant from domestic and Canadian sources and the China plant at the back of the Asian spot queue. Conventional builds still dominate because no 3 tesla sealed magnet is cleared. Both United States sites run winters under elevated grid ratings from 2027, and the helium cover thins each year because it is inventory bought at a 4 percent rate against rising prices.

path.sentence: The truce is renewed at its notice date, the Gulf route stays near closed, and a container fleet with a 35 to 48 day hold sets the helium cover at the United States plant while the Carolinas grid is rated elevated from 2027.
Conventional builds still dominate, the Midcontinent grid is rated high from the winter of 2028, and the helium cover thins each budget round as rates and input prices stay up.

what_fails_first.sentence: The United States magnet plant runs out of helium on hand first. A winter power curtailment or a flood cuts power to the liquefier and closes the trailer road while the next helium container is still in transit, and the helium on hand runs out before the delivery arrives.
what_fails_first.tag: Placeholder on the days of cover; Panel judgement on the path

futures.how_soon: The failure comes in the winter of 2028 to 2029. A storm as severe as the 2018 inland flood could bring it forward to any hurricane season from 2027. The China plant's helium allocation queue is the second to fail, pushing Asian installs more than 30 days late in the first half of 2028.
futures.what_it_costs: The United States magnet plant stops once for 30 to 45 days, and a quarter of Western Hemisphere installs run more than 30 days late (panel estimate). Asian installs run late on the allocation schedule. Market share does not move, because every supplier is short of helium at the same time.
futures.what_prevents_it: Logistics keeps more days of helium on hand at the United States plant than a container's hold time plus the 10 days the grid took to rebuild after the 2024 storm. Site operations puts the liquefier on backup power separate from the plant's power feed. Both must be in place before the winter of 2028, so both start by the second quarter of 2027.

how_sure.basis: the fleet of helium containers, the hold time, the grid ratings and the allocation letters come from dated public sources, but no grid warning has yet led to a curtailment lasting weeks, the days of helium on hand are a Placeholder, and the panel split six to five on which plant fails first.

futures.what_would_change_this: A 3 tesla sealed magnet cleared for sale, or the Gulf route reopening, moves the line toward Future 2. A United States helium allocation rule moves it toward Future 3. A confirmed figure of more than 60 days of helium on hand at the United States plant removes that failure, and the China plant's helium queue becomes the first to fail.

futures.name: Trade costs rise and sealed magnets end the helium limit
futures.sentence: Trade rules raise costs but cut nothing off, and by 2031 helium no longer decides whether a magnet ships. The one part that keeps every magnet cold, the cold head, then comes from a single maker.
futures.what_happens: The truce is renewed and parts flow at a tariff cost. The Gulf route reopens and the allocation letters stop. Sealed 1.5 tesla magnets build service history and European tenders pull sealed designs. A 3 tesla sealed magnet is cleared, the test draw proves to be a cylinder, and sealed designs take most new builds and the European replacement wave. The magnet is still wound from one mill's wire, and one Japanese cold head now carries the whole thermal load of every new magnet with no helium reserve behind it.

path.sentence: The truce is renewed, the Gulf route reopens to insured traffic, and sealed 1.5 tesla magnets cleared at three makers build service history while European tenders pull sealed designs.
A 3 tesla sealed magnet is cleared, sealed designs take most new builds, helium becomes a service matter, and the plant floor changes trade from helium handling to vacuum and cryocooler work.

what_fails_first.sentence: Cold heads fail first. One maker supplies both new builds and the spare cold heads for installed sealed magnets, which warm up when a cold head fails, so an earthquake or a plant outage at the maker stops both magnet plants at once.
what_fails_first.tag: Panel judgement; the maker's location is AI-suggested and Engineering confirms it against the Nankai Trough zone

futures.how_soon: The risk opens once sealed magnets pass half of output, which the panel expects in 2029, and lasts to 2031. The event itself has no schedule.
futures.what_it_costs: Both plants stop for more than 30 days, because they share the cold head and requalifying a new source takes 18 months, longer than any inventory lasts. Installed sealed magnets that lose a cold head warm up while service and new builds compete for the part, so hospitals face a scanner that cannot run rather than a late install.
futures.what_prevents_it: Engineering and Sourcing qualify a second cold-head maker for the sealed design before sealed magnets pass half of output, or Engineering builds in a tested hold that keeps a magnet cold for 30 days without a working cold head. Either must start by mid-2027, because requalification takes 18 months.

how_sure.basis: wire and the cold head are sole-source parts today, and the panel was most sure that this will not change by 2031. It was less sure that a cold-head outage stops the line rather than only costing money, and least sure of the date, because the trigger has no schedule.

futures.what_would_change_this: A second cold-head maker cleared for the sealed design before 2029 means a cold-head outage costs money but stays inside the 30-day limit. A sealed-magnet test draw the size of a full helium delivery pulls this future back toward Future 1. If no 3 tesla sealed magnet is cleared by 2028, this future moves beyond 2031.

futures.name: A part is cut off and helium still limits shipments
futures.sentence: A government cuts off a part before 2031 while magnets still need helium to ship. The stop falls on the China plant, inside a trading partner's borders, and the United States plant cannot cover for it.
futures.what_happens: The truce lapses at its notice date and entity listings in 2027 name the China plant's logic supplier and a cryogenic parts route. The Gulf route stays near closed, so helium at both plants is bought on allocation letters. Two blocs harden. The China plant builds for Asia without United States-origin logic, the United States plant keeps shipping on allocated helium but cannot cover Asia because its ramp and test capacity is sized for one hemisphere, and payment rails and customs become a licence queue.

path.sentence: The truce lapses at its notice date, entity listings in 2027 name the China plant's logic supplier and a cryogenic parts route, and helium at both plants stays on allocation.
Two blocs harden, the China plant builds for Asia without United States-origin logic, its lanes to Japan and India run under grey-zone pressure, and payment rails split by bloc.

what_fails_first.sentence: The China plant fails first. It sits inside a trading partner's borders and holds weeks, not months, of programmable logic parts, so an entity listing of its logic supplier stops the control electronics for every system it builds.
what_fails_first.tag: AI-suggested on what the plant imports and how much it holds; Sourcing confirms

futures.how_soon: The stop comes within one quarter of the first entity listing, inside the 2027 sourcing cycle. The panel's first estimate is the second half of 2027. An investigation under China's amended cyber law, combined with a freeze on payments, could cause the same stop sooner.
futures.what_it_costs: The China plant stops for more than 30 days, and no other plant can cover Asia. Asian installs run more than 30 days late for two quarters or more, and market share moves in Japan and India because a China-built competitor keeps delivering. The United States plant's helium on hand runs out second, by early 2028.
futures.what_prevents_it: Sourcing holds more logic and cold-head stock at the China plant than the export license queue takes to clear, bought before the truce notice date. Engineering qualifies a source of logic parts that does not originate in the United States for the Asian build, starting by the first quarter of 2027.

how_sure.basis: the listing tools exist and were used on this sector in 2025, and geography decides which plant a listing strands. The date rests on the truce notice and on an export license approval rate that is not published.

futures.what_would_change_this: If the truce is renewed at its notice date and no listing names the plant or its suppliers, this future fades. A listing that names cold heads before logic parts moves the first failure to the cold head and delays it by a quarter. If the Gulf route reopens, this future affects only one hemisphere.

futures.name: A part is cut off and sealed magnets end the helium limit
futures.sentence: Sealed magnets take most new builds while export controls restrict trade. The stop falls on the cold head, which now keeps every magnet cold.
futures.what_happens: The truce lapses and the first measures are tariffs and a listing on control logic that the China plant absorbs with stock raised after the notice. The Gulf route reopens and helium becomes a cost line. Sealed magnets take most new builds and a 3 tesla clearance arrives by 2028. United States hospitals defer orders in 2027 and the OEM slips down its suppliers' queues. The cold-head maker's parent, for whom MR is a minority of revenue, fills its order book with fusion, physics and quantum work, and a producer-country notice lists 4 kelvin cryocoolers as dual use, closing the licence route for the China plant just as Europe's replacement orders rise.

path.sentence: The truce lapses, tariffs and a logic listing are absorbed with stock, the Gulf route reopens, sealed magnets take most new builds and a 3 tesla clearance arrives by 2028 while United States hospitals defer orders.

The cold-head maker's parent allocates capacity to better-paying buyers, a producer-country notice lists cryocoolers as dual use, and Europe's replacement peak lands on a line with no cold heads and no helium fallback.

what_fails_first.sentence: Cold heads fail first. The parent company of the only qualified maker gives its capacity to buyers who pay more, an export-control listing removes the license route, and every magnet shipped or in the field depends on the part.
what_fails_first.tag: AI-suggested; Engineering confirms the maker's location and ownership, Sourcing confirms the parent's MR share

futures.how_soon: The failure comes by 2029. Lead times pass 30 days within a quarter of the parent's allocation letter, and a second maker takes 18 months to qualify, so the gap runs into 2030.
futures.what_it_costs: Both plants stop for more than 30 days, for most of 18 months. Every install in the backlog runs more than 30 days late, installed sealed magnets miss their service commitments because they warm up without a spare cold head, and the delays fall on the European replacement peak, so market share moves to competitors. This is the most expensive of the four futures.
futures.what_prevents_it: Engineering and Sourcing qualify a second cold-head maker before 2029, which means starting by the second quarter of 2027. Sourcing signs a multi-year supply agreement with the parent company in the 2027 sourcing cycle.

how_sure.basis: the single source, the parent's revenue mix and the 18-month requalification come from round 1 of the panel's research, and eight of the 11 panel members point to the cold head as the first to fail. The date rests on an allocation nobody has announced and an export-control listing that does not exist yet.

futures.what_would_change_this: A producer-country notice naming wire before cryocoolers (a related cooling part) moves the first failure to the wire. If no 3 tesla sealed magnet is cleared by 2028, this future merges into Future 3. If the parent company announces the sale or closure of the cold-head plant, the date moves to the announcement.

indicators.name: Federal Register actions naming the parts
indicators.what_is_measured: Any proclamation or Commerce rule naming finished MR scanners, superconducting wire, niobium, cryocoolers or cold heads, including the Section 232 medical equipment investigation opened 26 September 2025.
indicators.settles_a_when: The 2027 sourcing cycle closes with no document naming the parts, and the Section 232 medical action is confined to finished scanners or lapses.
indicators.settles_b_when: A document names wire, niobium, cryocoolers or cold heads, or a proclamation imposes a quota or licence on MR parts; the stop reaches N03, N05 or N17 within a quarter.
indicators.false_signal: Silence. A Section 232 report goes to the President unpublished, so no proclamation can mean a decision pending rather than no decision. An edit to the existing superconducting materials entry is not a new listing.
indicators.last_read: On 11 Oct 2026 no Bureau of Industry and Security document named the parts, and there was no Section 232 proclamation on medical products.

indicators.name: Additions to the United States Entity List (the export blacklist)
indicators.what_is_measured: Bureau of Industry and Security rules adding parties, read for the China plant, its logic supplier, a cryogenic parts route or a Chinese wire mill.
indicators.source_name: Federal Register documents interface, Bureau of Industry and Security
indicators.cadence: On publication, several rules a quarter
indicators.settles_a_when: The truce notice renews with no addition touching medical electronics or cryogenic parts by the close of the 2027 sourcing cycle.
indicators.settles_b_when: A rule names the plant, its logic supplier or a logic distributor serving China; the stop follows within a quarter (future F3).
indicators.false_signal: A rule that only removes parties, or adds defence end users unrelated to imaging.
indicators.last_read: The newest action, on 24 Aug 2026, removed companies only. No addition touches the OEM's sites or suppliers.

indicators.name: China trade truce notice and Chinese counter-listings
indicators.what_is_measured: Whether the suspension of China's 24 percent additional tariff is renewed at its notice date, and whether a Ministry of Commerce announcement adds a wire mill, the cold-head maker, the OEM or a foreign-owned imaging plant to an export-control or unreliable-entity list.
indicators.source_name: State Council Tariff Commission notices and Ministry of Commerce announcements, read through wire reports and a law firm's tracker
indicators.cadence: Event driven; several announcements a month, checked quarterly
indicators.settles_a_when: The suspension is renewed for a year or longer and no 2026 or 2027 announcement names cryogenic or superconducting items or an imaging plant.
indicators.settles_b_when: The 24 percent duty returns, or an announcement names a cryocooler or wire maker or a foreign-owned imaging plant, or extends dual-use controls to cold heads bound for China.
indicators.false_signal: Quota and anti-dumping announcements, and batches that stay on defence firms.
indicators.last_read: The tariff suspension has been in force since 10 Nov 2025 for one year, and no renewal notice was found. China's Ministry of Commerce Announcement No. 46 of 9 Oct 2026 contains no export-control item. Two earlier sources give the truce end date as 10 Nov 2026 or 10 Jan 2027.

indicators.name: Filings by the sole suppliers' parent companies
indicators.what_is_measured: Filings and press releases by the listed parents of the qualified wire mill and the two cryocooler makers, read for a sale, closure or market exit of the superconductor or cryocooler unit, and for how much of the backlog is fusion or physics work.
indicators.source_name: United States Securities and Exchange Commission company filings; the owners' press release pages
indicators.cadence: Within four days of an event for the listed parent; quarterly read of the press pages
indicators.settles_a_when: The 2027 sourcing cycle closes with no disposal and both parents still offer the MR part.
indicators.settles_b_when: A filing or release announces a sale or closure of the unit, or restricts it to research markets; this is the owner-exit route to a stop in futures F4 and F2.
indicators.false_signal: A backlog rise or a segment reshuffle that changes nothing on the shop floor.
indicators.last_read: No sale had been filed on 11 Oct 2026. The United States cryocooler maker that could have been a second source was bought in 2023 and its output turned to research (a fixed fact from round 1 of the panel's research). Sourcing still owes the link to the Japanese parent's investor relations page.

indicators.name: Export port closures and the longshore labor contract
indicators.what_is_measured: Dated closure advisories from the one export port, major work stoppages at ports and carriers, and the status of the longshore master contract expiring 30 September 2030.
indicators.source_name: Port authority advisories; Bureau of Labor Statistics work stoppages; the longshore union's site
indicators.cadence: Per event, daily in a storm; monthly stoppages file
indicators.settles_a_when: Closures stay at days through 2031 and the 2030 contract is renewed before expiry.
indicators.settles_b_when: One closure or stoppage at the port, the oversize carriers or the gas carriers runs past 30 days, or 30 September 2030 passes with no agreement.
indicators.false_signal: An inland-yard or gate-hours notice; a short strike with large headcount, such as the three-day port strike of October 2024.
indicators.last_read: There has been no weather closure in 2026, and the newest advisory is a gate-hours notice of 23 Sep 2026. The longshore contract was approved on 7 Feb 2025 and runs to 30 Sep 2030.

indicators.name: European Union rule on the origin of medical devices in public tenders
indicators.what_is_measured: The status of Regulation (EU) 2025/1197, which bars Chinese-origin medical devices from tenders at or above 5 million euros, and any widening, counter-measure or withdrawal.
indicators.source_name: EUR-Lex, the European Union's law database
indicators.settles_a_when: The measure stays at its threshold or is withdrawn after a settlement; nothing stops.
indicators.settles_b_when: The threshold is removed, the measure extends to components, or a Chinese counter-rule bars foreign-built MR systems from Chinese hospitals.
indicators.false_signal: A European preference clause in the procurement directives, which scores origin rather than barring it.
indicators.last_read: The rule has been in force since 20 Jun 2025 for tenders of €5 million or more. The page was empty when fetched on 11 Oct 2026, so this reading comes from round 1 of the panel's research.

indicators.name: Daily ship crossings of the Gulf strait
indicators.what_is_measured: Ships broadcasting through the Strait of Hormuz each day, the lane Gulf helium leaves by, against a typical 85 a day.
indicators.source_name: International Monetary Fund PortWatch, republished by straits.live
indicators.cadence: Daily rows, published weekly, last three days open to revision
indicators.settles_a_when: The count stays below about 40 a day through 2028 and war-risk cover stays withdrawn, or a United States allocation rule arrives.
indicators.settles_b_when: The count holds above about 70 a day for two consecutive quarters, insured container traffic resumes and allocation letters stop.
indicators.false_signal: A one-week jump from convoyed tankers. The count is all ships, not helium carriers; transits can recover while Qatar's liquefaction is still being rebuilt.
indicators.last_read: Four ships crossed on 4 Oct 2026, against a typical 85 a day.

indicators.name: Helium price and where United States imports come from
indicators.what_is_measured: The posted Grade-A base price per cubic metre and United States import shares by origin from the annual survey; the quarterly bulk contract price by region under allocation; the producer price index for industrial gases.
indicators.source_name: United States Geological Survey Mineral Commodity Summaries, helium chapter; IMARC Group bulk helium price index; Bureau of Labor Statistics series PCU325120325120
indicators.cadence: Annual in February; quarterly for the bulk index; monthly for the producer index
indicators.settles_a_when: The base price rises two editions running with surcharges still posted, the Qatari share falls further, and the United States bulk price holds above 100,000 dollars a tonne through 2027.
indicators.settles_b_when: The surcharge sentence disappears, the base price falls two editions running, and the bulk price falls two quarters running with spot availability.
indicators.false_signal: A lower posted base price with surcharges still posted, because allocation lives in the surcharge. A producer-index fall driven by argon and oxygen.
indicators.last_read: Helium cost about $12 per cubic meter in 2025, down from $14 in 2024, with surcharges posted. Canada supplied 47% and Qatar 28% of United States imports from 2021 to 2024 (United States Geological Survey, Feb 2026, from round 1 of the panel's research). The producer price index rose 5.4% in the year to August 2026.

indicators.name: A United States helium export or allocation rule
indicators.what_is_measured: Any Federal Register rule or presidential document naming helium with export, allocation or Section 232.
indicators.settles_a_when: A rule is proposed or signed; it also moves U1 toward a stop for the China plant, which cannot buy Chinese helium.
indicators.settles_b_when: None appears while Gulf transits recover.
indicators.false_signal: A Bureau of Land Management lease or royalty notice naming helium, which is land administration.
indicators.last_read: No rule existed on 11 Oct 2026. The feed address follows the confirmed pattern for the Federal Register interface, but it was not fetched this round.

indicators.name: Sealed magnets in new United States clearances for sale
indicators.what_is_measured: New 510(k) clearances in product code LNH (magnetic resonance diagnostic device), read for the first 3 tesla sealed magnet and for the sealed share of new clearances.
indicators.source_name: Device clearance data from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) through openFDA; FDA 510(k) premarket clearance summaries
indicators.cadence: Weekly refresh; quarterly read of each summary's cryostat section
indicators.settles_a_when: No 3 tesla sealed clearance appears by the 2027 sourcing cycle and sealed designs stay a minority through 2028.
indicators.settles_b_when: A 3 tesla sealed clearance lands, sealed designs pass half of new clearances in a rolling year, and Engineering confirms the test draw as a cylinder (Placeholder).
indicators.false_signal: A 3 tesla clearance for a software or coil change on a conventional platform; several K numbers for one platform family; a run of low-field or portable clearances, which feed the fifth-future watch row rather than end B.
indicators.last_read: There were 21 clearances in 2026 up to 16 Sep. Five name a sealed or helium-light magnet housing, all at or below 1.5 tesla, and none is a 3 tesla sealed magnet.

series.basis: sealed or helium-light records among 21 LNH clearances in 2026, read from summaries

indicators.name: A second source of cold heads that reach 4 kelvin
indicators.what_is_measured: Whether any maker other than the sole Japanese group lists a 4 kelvin Gifford-McMahon cold head, which settles the six-to-five split on whether the cold head breaks or costs when helium no longer decides.
indicators.source_name: Product pages of the United States cryocooler maker on the OEM's supplier map
indicators.settles_a_when: No second 4 kelvin Gifford-McMahon source exists, so at end B the cold head is a single point with no spare design.
indicators.settles_b_when: A second maker lists a 4 kelvin cold head, or a sealed magnet is cleared on a pulse-tube cooler.
indicators.false_signal: A 4 kelvin pulse-tube cryostat on the same page, which is not a drop-in cold head.
indicators.last_read: On 11 Oct 2026 the second maker listed Gifford-McMahon coolers only at 20 to 80 kelvin, and it reached 4 kelvin only with a pulse-tube cooler. It is not a drop-in second source.

indicators.name: Winter grid rating at the two United States sites
indicators.what_is_measured: The winter risk rating and extreme-scenario reserve margin for the regions covering the magnet plant and the hub.
indicators.source_name: North American Electric Reliability Corporation, Winter Reliability Assessment
indicators.cadence: Annual, each November; read each quarter against the plant's backup-power Placeholder
indicators.settles_a_when: A region is rated high and a multi-week curtailment reaches the plant while the Gulf is still impaired, because the liquefier stops and helium cover becomes the margin.
indicators.settles_b_when: It cannot settle end B; a normal rating only removes one route to end A.
indicators.false_signal: A cold-snap advisory that lifts in days.
indicators.last_read: The January 2026 long-term assessment rates the Carolinas grid elevated from 2027 and the Midcontinent grid high from the winter of 2028. The link used is the 2025 winter assessment.

actions.name: Confirm the Placeholder numbers the results rest on
actions.owner: Logistics, Site operations, Engineering and Sourcing
actions.protects: It protects against every risk. Six internal figures decide whether the first failure in each future is real: days of helium on hand at the United States plant, the plant's backup power, the helium a sealed magnet draws in testing (in liters), where the cold-head maker and the wire mill sit relative to the Nankai Trough earthquake zone off Japan, the weeks of logic parts held at the China plant, and the price at which the OEM loses its helium allocation.
actions.why_now: Every other action is sized from these numbers, and all of them are synthetic today. All 11 panel members ranked this action first or second.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once the 2027 sourcing cycle opens on synthetic numbers.
actions.act_if: Act now, and ask again any function that has not returned its number by the end of 2026.
actions.pause_if: Do not pause this action.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if a confirmed number moves a first failure by a quarter, or shows that a failure costs money but stays inside the 30-day limit.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means a year of decisions sized on guesses and a capital plan built on synthetic numbers.

actions.name: Test a 30-day manual fallback at both plants and both sole suppliers against a 35-day systems outage
actions.owner: Site operations with Sourcing, with the wire mill and the cold-head maker taking part
actions.protects: It protects the United States plant, the China plant, the wire mill, the cold-head maker, the gas carriers and the port terminal. A 35-day systems outage is the one failure that every future shares, and it falls wherever each future's first failure already sits.
actions.why_now: No outside event will warn of the shared failure, so the test sets the only deadline. All 11 panel members say it works in every future. The people who ran the line on paper are the ones nearest retirement.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the first outage, or once the people who can write the manual procedure have retired.
actions.act_if: Act if any site cannot say today how it would ship without its systems, or if a sole supplier or a peer in the sector reports a systems outage of a week or more.
actions.pause_if: Pause once a site has passed a timed test twice.
actions.look_again_if: Look again after any systems migration, if a test fails, or if the drill assumed the grid and the roads were working.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves another year in which a 35-day stop pushes the line past the 30-day limit in every future. The stop is largely uninsured, because cyber insurance excludes acts by states.

actions.name: Qualify a second cold-head maker
actions.protects: It protects the cold head, and through it both plants and the installed scanners. It removes the first failure in Future 2 and Future 4, and it reduces the cost of a cold-head outage in Future 1 and Future 3, where helium is the fallback. Four panel members (Foreign trade and payments, Geopolitical, Technology shift and Contrarian) say it works in all four futures, because the same cold head also cools conventional magnets. The other seven limit it to the futures where sealed magnets take over.
actions.why_now: Requalification takes 18 months, and in Future 4 the cold heads fail by 2029, so a start after mid-2027 comes too late. The Contrarian member's condition stands: one maker has already left the market, so the action becomes real only once Sourcing names a second maker with a letter of intent.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the end of 2027.
actions.act_if: Act if Sourcing names a second maker with a letter of intent, if sealed magnets pass a quarter of new clearances, or if a producer country's export-control register names cryocoolers or cold heads.
actions.pause_if: Pause if no second maker exists, and switch to the supply agreement (A2) and the 30-day hold (A7) instead. Also pause if sealed magnets stay below a quarter of clearances in 2028 and conventional builds still dominate.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if the parent company announces a review or exit of its cryogenics unit, if a second maker sits inside the same Nankai Trough earthquake zone, or if the cold head's own suppliers are shared (A24).
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means the second source arrives after the Future 4 failure and after a tender cycle. In Future 4 both plants stay stopped into 2030.

actions.name: Keep an offline, restore-tested copy of the design and qualification record
actions.principle: Resilient products and processes (intellectual property ownership and continuity)
actions.protects: It protects the design and qualification record, and through it every 18-month requalification of a site or supplier. Every future assumes the record is intact, and nothing on the starting list of actions kept it that way.
actions.why_now: The Security and Contrarian members proposed it independently. Losing the record would make every replacement time unknown, and the manual fallback test (A9) works only if the record survives.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the first systems outage.
actions.act_if: Act if nobody has ever timed a restore of the record.
actions.pause_if: Pause if a timed restore within 30 days already exists.
actions.look_again_if: Look again after any cyber attack on the OEM or a sole supplier.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves the assumption that every future rests on unchecked for another year.

actions.name: Keep more days of helium on hand at the United States plant than a container's hold time plus the 10-day grid rebuild
actions.protects: It protects the United States plant and its helium on hand. It removes the first failure in Future 1 and the second failure in Future 3. In Future 2 and Future 4 it only adds carrying cost.
actions.why_now: In Future 1 the helium runs out in the winter of 2028 to 2029, and it could happen in any hurricane season from 2027. Helium stock builds slowly at allocated volumes and cannot be bought once the shortage starts. On 11 Oct 2026 the indicators lean toward the two futures where this action pays off.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the 2028 hurricane season.
actions.act_if: Act if Logistics reports fewer days of helium on hand than a container's hold time plus 10 days, if Gulf strait traffic stays below a quarter of normal into 2027, or if an allocation letter cuts the plant's monthly volume.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the Gulf strait reopens to insured shipping and the allocation letters stop.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if a United States helium allocation rule is proposed, if a sealed magnet's test draw is confirmed as one gas cylinder, or if the extra test capacity in A8 raises the plant's helium use.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks one 30 to 45 day stop at the United States plant and a quarter of Western installs arriving late (panel estimate).

actions.name: Put the liquefier at the United States plant on backup power separate from the plant's power feed
actions.protects: It protects the United States plant and its helium on hand. It covers the most ordinary failure on the map of sites and suppliers, a winter power curtailment, and it does no harm in the other futures.
actions.why_now: The grid reliability body rates the Carolinas grid elevated from 2027 and the Midcontinent grid high from the winter of 2028. A generator takes a year to procure, and data centers are buying the same units. The Contrarian member warns that the panel will underrate this action because it is small.
actions.start_by: In the 2027 capital plan, with procurement by mid-2027
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the winter of 2028.
actions.act_if: Act if Site operations confirms that the liquefier shares the plant's power feed, or if the grid operator issues a winter curtailment notice for the region.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the power feed is reclassified as a critical load, or if the plant holds more than 60 days of helium on hand.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if sealed magnets pass half of output, if the switchgear can be reached from the plant network, or if the backup fuel supply crosses the feed's flood zone.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks a winter in which the liquefier sits idle through the first curtailment.

actions.name: Hold more logic and cold-head stock at the China plant than the export license queue takes to clear
actions.protects: It protects the China plant and its supply of logic parts and cold heads. It is the only action that has to move before Question 1 is answered, and it has the nearest deadline on the list.
actions.why_now: The panel's first reading of the truce notice date is 10 Nov 2026. Stock bought after an export-control listing may itself need an export license. Three panel members add Future 4, where the stock absorbs a listing of the logic parts.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once an entity listing names the plant or its logic supplier.
actions.act_if: Act if the truce is not renewed at its notice date, or if a listing names any supplier to the China plant.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the truce is renewed for a year or more with no listing.
actions.look_again_if: Look again once Sourcing states the stock in weeks, if the license queue shortens, or if the warehouse sits in the flood plain.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means that in Future 3 the plant fails with empty shelves, and the stop lasts the whole license queue.

actions.name: Sign a multi-year supply agreement with the cold-head maker's parent company, with a change-of-control clause and step-in rights to tooling and drawings
actions.protects: It protects the supply of cold heads if the parent company sells or leaves the business. Nine panel members limit it to Future 4, because a contract changes neither an export license nor a flood. The Financial member says it works in all four futures if it carries a change-of-control clause.
actions.why_now: The 2027 sourcing cycle is the last normal negotiation before the parent's next capacity review. A single sale document could end the line.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once the parent announces a sale, a review or an exit.
actions.act_if: Act if the parent's filings show its cryogenics unit shrinking, under review or below the group's margin.
actions.pause_if: Pause if A1 qualifies a second maker, or if the parent invests in the plant.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if a listing names cryocoolers, if the parent changes hands, or if the yen moves more than 15% against the dollar.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means negotiating from a queue, and in Future 4 the whole gap is left uncovered.

actions.name: Confirm the export-control classifications of wire, cold heads and logic parts, and the China plant's export license approval rate
actions.protects: It protects the wire, the cold heads, the logic parts and the China plant. Future 3 and Future 4 rest on export classifications nobody has checked, and magnet-grade wire has never been checked against the dual-use export lists.
actions.why_now: It costs nothing, and it decides whether the China plant stock (A5) and the second logic source (A6) are sound bets or wasted money. The Geopolitical and Foreign trade and payments members proposed it independently.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the truce notice date.
actions.act_if: Act now, whatever the indicators show.
actions.pause_if: Do not pause this action.
actions.look_again_if: Look again at every revision of the export-control lists.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means A5 and A6 are bought against a guess, and the only wire source sits under a rule nobody has read.

actions.name: Run an annual credit and ownership watch on the wire mill and the cold-head parent
actions.protects: It protects the wire and the cold head. Question 1 counts an owner leaving the business as a stop, and an exit shows up in filings before it reaches the press.
actions.why_now: It costs very little. The cold-head parent's share of revenue from MR is itself a Placeholder.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once a sale is announced.
actions.act_if: Act if either parent's revenue from the relevant business falls under 5% of the group's revenue.
actions.pause_if: Do not pause this action.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if ownership changes.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means an exit is seen in the press instead of in the filings a year earlier.

actions.name: Test one hazard against several sites at once: one hurricane against the plant, the port and the helium shipping routes together, and one Nankai Trough earthquake against the cold-head and compressor makers together
actions.protects: It protects the United States plant, the export port, the gas carriers, the oversize road route, the cold-head maker and the compressor maker. The starting list of actions tested sites one at a time, and weather does not strike one site at a time.
actions.why_now: The continuity plan tests sites one at a time. One Atlantic storm can close three sites in a month.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the 2027 hurricane season.
actions.act_if: Act if the continuity plan still tests sites one at a time.
actions.pause_if: Do not pause this action.
actions.look_again_if: Look again after each named storm.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves a season exposed to a stop that single-site plans do not see.

actions.name: Qualify a source of logic parts that does not originate in the United States for the Asian build
actions.protects: It protects the supply of logic parts and the China plant. It shortens the Future 3 stop rather than preventing it, because 18 months from early 2027 ends at or after the failure, and a part made abroad can still be caught by the United States foreign direct product rule. Five panel members add Future 4, where it shortens the license queue. The Contrarian member notes that it gives up some ownership of the design.
actions.why_now: Only a start in the first quarter of 2027 finishes before 2029.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after mid-2027.
actions.act_if: Act if an entity listing names the China plant's logic supplier, or if export license approvals stay below half for two quarters.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the truce is renewed with no listing, or if the China plant stock (A5) covers the license queue.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if the foreign direct product rule reaches this product class, or if a second chip foundry clears equivalent parts.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year gives a 2029 answer to a 2027 failure, and the Future 3 stop runs the whole license queue.

actions.name: Size ramp-up and test capacity at the United States plant to cover part of the Asian build
actions.owner: Site operations with the Install PMO
actions.protects: It protects the China plant's customers. It is the only action that keeps an Asian delivery date when the China plant stops. It does nothing in Future 1, where the United States plant itself fails, and it raises that plant's helium use, so the 2027 capital plan must size it together with the helium stock (A3).
actions.why_now: Capacity takes 24 months to change (AI-suggested, Site operations to confirm), and the 2027 capital plan is the only chance to fund it. The Financial member judged that it ties up more working capital than any other action on the list.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after 2028.
actions.act_if: Act if a listing names the China plant or its logic supplier, or if the plant's stock falls below the length of the license queue.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the truce is renewed through 2028, or if a second Asian site is approved.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if the helium on hand cannot carry the extra use, if there are not enough technicians to staff a second shift, or if Asian tenders add local-content rules.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year loses an Asian tender cycle, and in Future 3 the route that would supply Asia is not ready for two more years.

actions.name: Design and test a hold that keeps a sealed magnet cold for 30 days without a working cold head
actions.protects: It protects the cold head and the installed sealed magnets. The Contrarian member notes that the physics may not allow it, so the first step is a cheap study.
actions.why_now: It matters once sealed magnets pass half of output, which the panel expects in 2029.
actions.start_by: With a study in 2027 and the design by 2028
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once sealed magnets pass half of output.
actions.act_if: Act if sealed magnets pass a quarter of new builds, or if the study shows that a hold of more than 30 days is possible.
actions.pause_if: Pause if A1 qualifies a second maker, or if the study shows a hold of under 10 days.
actions.look_again_if: Look again when Engineering states the test draw, or if a conduction-cooled design appears in clearances.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting costs little until 2028. After that, each year leaves the sealed magnets in the field with no hold.

actions.name: Build a skilled-trades hiring pipeline at the United States plant before the sealed-magnet conversion decision (A11)
actions.protects: It protects the technicians and the United States plant. Competence takes 18 months to build, and nobody has measured when the current technicians will retire. A skill that has retired cannot be bought back the way a part can.
actions.why_now: The conventional and sealed lines need different skilled trades, and hiring for 2029 starts in 2027.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after 2028.
actions.act_if: Act if more than a quarter of magnet winders and cryogenic technicians will retire within five years.
actions.pause_if: Pause if automation takes winding off the factory floor.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if a competing local employer closes.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means a group of new hires who are not competent until 2030.

actions.name: Map labor contract expiry dates at the plants, the hub and the ports against storm and winter seasons
actions.protects: It protects the plants, the hub and the export port. The longshore master contract expires on 30 Sep 2030, inside the hurricane season, and a port contract expiring in a storm month means two stops at once.
actions.why_now: It takes a week of work and needs nothing to be bought.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late at the next port contract expiry.
actions.act_if: Act if any contract expires in 2027 or 2028.
actions.pause_if: Do not pause this action.
actions.look_again_if: Look again every year.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year lets a known date arrive without a plan.

actions.name: Rewrite delivery clauses, agree a late-delivery remedy script and publish delivery performance before health systems do
actions.owner: Install PMO (project management office) with the S&OP (sales and operations planning) council
actions.protects: It protects market share. It changes what a late install costs, not whether it happens, and all four futures push installs past the 30-day limit somewhere. No public tender framework that the panel retrieved scores delivery reliability explicitly, so whether tenders score late delivery at all is unverified.
actions.why_now: Hospital purchasing frameworks renew on multi-year cycles.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once a health system publishes delivery scores first.
actions.act_if: Act if a large customer adds delivery scoring.
actions.pause_if: Pause if tenders never score reliability.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if competitors publish their delivery performance first.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves a cycle of delivery scores the OEM does not manage, and the market share lost at the first install more than 30 days late.

actions.name: Set an allocation rule for scarce magnets
actions.protects: It protects market share where the OEM is one of two or three suppliers. In every future it changes the cost of a stop, not whether the stop happens.
actions.why_now: Without a rule, the first stop will allocate scarce magnets by order date.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after the first stop.
actions.act_if: Act if any plant stops.
actions.pause_if: Do not pause this action.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if tender scoring changes.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means the first stop allocates magnets by order date.

actions.name: Pre-permit an oversize road route to a second export port and hold helium there before each hurricane season
actions.protects: It protects the export port and the gas carriers. It reduces delays in all four futures, and it prevents a stop only in Future 1 and Future 3, where the helium held at the port matters.
actions.why_now: Hurricane season comes every year, and the single port closes for days in every future.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after a port closure of more than 10 days.
actions.act_if: Act if the port closes for 10 days, or if its records show a stop of more than 10 days.
actions.pause_if: Pause if a second berth is contracted, or if the helium on hand outlasts the longest closure.
actions.look_again_if: Look again after any bridge weight restriction on the route, or if the second port lies on the same storm track.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks a season of held exports.

actions.name: Contract a second carrier for liquid helium, with an inland transfer point
actions.protects: It protects the gas carriers and the helium on hand. A systems outage at a carrier uses up the helium on hand and stops the plant for 50 to 60 days (panel estimate).
actions.why_now: One carrier handles most deliveries (basis not stated).
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after a carrier outage.
actions.act_if: Act if one carrier handles more than two thirds of deliveries.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the plant holds 90 days of helium on hand.
actions.look_again_if: Look again every year.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves another year exposed to a carrier failure.

actions.name: Fix helium allocation priority in writing, indexed to a published price, on a shipping route that avoids the Gulf strait and sanctioned payment systems
actions.protects: It protects the helium supply and the helium on hand. The price at which the OEM loses its allocation is a Placeholder, and without a written priority the helium stock in A3 cannot be built at allocated volumes.
actions.why_now: A chip plant can take priority over the OEM at any time.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once a buyers' market returns or a chip plant takes priority.
actions.act_if: Act if a chip plant is reported taking priority, or if Qatar's share of United States helium imports falls further.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the Gulf strait reopens and a buyers' market returns.
actions.look_again_if: Look again at each allocation letter.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year could make the helium stock in A3 impossible to build.

actions.name: Hedge the yen exposure on cold heads and compressors for the contract term
actions.protects: It protects the bill for cold heads and compressors. It smooths costs in every future.
actions.why_now: It starts when the supply agreement (A2) is signed.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once the parent company reprices.
actions.act_if: Act if the Bank of Japan changes its interest rate path.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the supply agreement (A2) is priced in dollars.
actions.look_again_if: Look again every year.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year costs little.

actions.name: Map the cold head's own suppliers before signing a second maker
actions.protects: It protects the cold head. A second maker that relies on the same suppliers for regenerators and displacers (parts inside the cold head) gives only the appearance of a second source.
actions.why_now: It is a study of a few months, and the second maker (A1) should not be signed until it is done.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once A1 is signed.
actions.act_if: Act when A1 starts.
actions.pause_if: Pause if the maker shows that its inputs come from two sources.
actions.look_again_if: Look again at each qualification.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting means A1 may buy a second source that shares the first one's suppliers.

actions.name: Buy contingent business interruption insurance naming the wire mill, the cold-head maker and the helium supply
actions.protects: It pays toward the bill for a failure but does not prevent one, and only if insurers will write the policy. Cyber insurance already excludes acts by states.
actions.why_now: Insurers are withdrawing capacity for this kind of policy.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after a loss.
actions.act_if: Act if a broker quotes a policy that names the suppliers.
actions.pause_if: Pause if exclusions would void the policy.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if the premium costs more than the China plant stock in A5.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves one more year uninsured.

actions.name: Require counterfeit-avoidance and cyber attestation from sole suppliers and carriers
actions.protects: It protects the wire, the cold head, the electronics, the carriers and the port. Attestation must not replace the manual fallback exercise in A9.
actions.why_now: Future 4 adds the cost of grey-market cold heads, and attackers rarely get in through the OEM's own network.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late once a counterfeit part reaches a magnet.
actions.act_if: Act if a counterfeit alert names any kind of component on the supplier map.
actions.pause_if: Do not pause this action.
actions.look_again_if: Look again at each sourcing cycle.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means a year of unverified parts.

actions.name: Decide how fast the OEM converts to sealed magnets, including whether the 3 tesla line converts
actions.protects: This decision sets which pair of futures the line operates in. Converting trades a dependency on the Gulf (helium on hand) for one on Japan (the cold head). Waiting a year chooses Future 1 and Future 3 by default. Conversion makes A1 and A9 more valuable if it means one part keeps every magnet cold.
actions.why_now: The 2027 capital plan is the next chance to decide. The conventional and sealed lines need different skilled trades, and hiring for 2029 starts in 2027.
actions.too_late_after: It is too late after 2028.
actions.act_if: Act if a sealed magnet's test draw is confirmed as one gas cylinder and a 3 tesla sealed clearance is filed.
actions.pause_if: Pause if hospitals decline the first sealed option, if the test draw is the size of a full delivery, or if no second cold-head source exists.
actions.look_again_if: Look again if helium returns to a buyers' market, if a competitor gets a 3 tesla sealed magnet cleared, or if tenders score independence from helium.
actions.cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks hiring the wrong trades or none, and one more year on helium's terms.

brief.bottom_line: Every future stops this line somewhere before 2031, and in every one the first part to fail is a site or supplier already on the risk list. Three actions pay off in every future: confirm the internal numbers the results rest on, test a 30-day manual fallback at both plants and both sole suppliers, and start qualifying a second maker of cold heads (the part that keeps a magnet cold) by the second quarter of 2027.
brief.where_we_are_heading: On 11 Oct 2026 the indicators leaned toward trade costs rising without anything being cut off, and toward helium still limiting shipments. In the latest daily count, on 4 Oct 2026, four ships crossed the Gulf strait against a typical 85. Helium is bought on allocation letters, no export-control listing names wire or cold heads, and no 3 tesla sealed magnet has been cleared. Of the 12 indicators, 10 lean that way and two lean neither way. Neither question has been answered yet.
brief.what_fails_first: In the future the indicators lean toward, the United States magnet plant runs out of helium on hand first, in the winter of 2028 to 2029. A grid curtailment or a flood cuts power to the liquefier and closes the trailer road while the next container is still in transit. Any hurricane season from 2027 could bring this forward. The China plant's helium queue fails second, in the first half of 2028. If an export-control listing comes first, the China plant stops in the second half of 2027 because its supply of logic parts is cut off. If helium stops limiting shipments, a single Japanese cold head stops both plants.
brief.what_it_costs: In the future the indicators lean toward, the United States plant stops once for 30 to 45 days and a quarter of Western installs run more than 30 days late. Market share does not move, because every supplier is short of helium at the same time. The most expensive futures are the two where a part is cut off. In one, the China plant stops for the export license queue plus the time it takes to rehire, and Asian market share moves within one tender cycle. In the other, both plants stop for most of 18 months, installed magnets warm up, and Europe's replacement peak goes to competitors.
brief.right_in_every_future: Confirm the Placeholder numbers now: days of helium on hand, backup power, the helium a sealed magnet draws in testing (in liters), the China plant's logic stock in weeks, where the cold-head maker is located, and its parent company's share of revenue from MR. Test a 30-day manual fallback with the wire mill and the cold-head maker taking part, because a 35-day systems outage pushes the line past the 30-day limit in all four futures, wherever each future's first failure already sits. Keep an offline, restore-tested copy of the design record. Start qualifying a second cold-head maker by the second quarter of 2027, once Sourcing names one with a letter of intent.
brief.right_only_if_the_lean_holds: Keep more days of helium on hand at the United States plant than a container's hold time plus the 10-day grid rebuild, and put the liquefier on backup power, both before the winter of 2028. These pay off only in the futures where helium still limits shipments, which is where the indicators lean, and they only add carrying cost if sealed magnets take most new builds. Stock at the China plant is a bet on an export-control listing and must be bought before the truce notice, first read as 10 Nov 2026. A multi-year agreement with the cold-head maker's parent company is a bet on the parent leaving the business, and it does not help if an export license is refused.
brief.one_action_waiting: Confirm the Placeholder numbers. The work costs only phone calls, named owners in Logistics, Site operations, Engineering and Sourcing hold it, and until it is done every other action on this page is sized to a synthetic number.

evidence.claim: P1. Sealed, helium-light 1.5 tesla magnets are cleared products at three makers, cleared for the OEM's own platform on 5 February 2026. They still use niobium-titanium wire and a Gifford-McMahon cold head.
evidence.source: FDA K181479 (3 Aug 2018), K253779 (5 Feb 2026); technology lens
evidence.changes_if: A safety recall of the sealed class, or the OEM choosing not to convert its 3 tesla line. The conversion decision is the OEM's, not the world's.
evidence.confirm_by: No confirmation needed; dated public source

evidence.claim: P2. No 1.5 or 3 tesla magnet without niobium-titanium wire appears in United States clearance records to October 2026, and a new wire mill takes about 18 months to qualify, so wire stays the single most design-locked input through 2031.
evidence.source: openFDA read 11 Oct 2026; technology lens
evidence.changes_if: A high-temperature superconductor magnet cleared before 2028 and adopted at pace; no lens found evidence of either.
evidence.confirm_by: No confirmation needed; dated public source

evidence.claim: P3. Helium is a four-state market (United States 81, Qatar 63, Russia 18, Algeria 11 of 190 million cubic metres in 2025). Qatar's Ras Laffan complex was struck in March 2026, the energy minister put repairs at three to five years, Russian helium is barred from the United States and the European Union and self-licensed to 31 December 2027, Chinese helium is under an export ban with no end date, and the United States federal reserve was sold to a private firm on 27 June 2024. There is no public buffer anywhere.
evidence.source: USGS (Feb 2026); BLM (27 Jun 2024); Global Trade Alert; QatarEnergy statement via IOM3 (23 Mar 2026); geopolitical, financial, macroeconomic, infrastructure, foreign trade lenses
evidence.changes_if: Qatari helium units restarting much sooner than the minister's estimate. The macroeconomic lens notes a 6 March 2026 satellite analysis saying main equipment was intact and no producer disclosure confirms the helium units were hit. The repair timing is therefore moved to the uncertain list (U-H1).
evidence.confirm_by: No confirmation needed; dated public source

evidence.claim: P4. The United States magnet plant sits inside the only helium producer that is a net exporter. Qatar's share of United States helium imports fell from 40 to 28 percent and Canada's rose from 36 to 47 percent across the 2020 to 2024 windows, and the base price fell. The United States plant and the China plant face different helium worlds.
evidence.source: USGS (Jan 2025, Feb 2026); contrarian, geopolitical lenses
evidence.changes_if: A United States export control or allocation rule on helium, or a Cliffside or Hugoton outage coinciding with the Gulf outage.
evidence.confirm_by: No confirmation needed; dated public source

evidence.claim: P5. Helium moves in a fleet of roughly 500 to 700 40-foot ISO containers that hold liquid for about 35 to 48 days, with one maker behind most of them.
evidence.source: Linde product page (read 11 Oct 2026); consultancy analysis (1 Apr 2026), AI-suggested on fleet size
evidence.changes_if: A second container maker at scale, or a shift to air-shipped dewars; neither found.
evidence.confirm_by: No confirmation needed; dated public source

evidence.claim: P6. Niobium is 93 percent Brazilian from one family-controlled private producer; the United States is wholly import dependent; China takes 49 percent of Brazil's ferroniobium exports. Leverage on wire sits with one producer state and one dominant buyer and reaches the OEM through the mill, not the ore.
evidence.source: USGS (Feb 2026); geopolitical, financial, foreign trade lenses
evidence.changes_if: A Canadian or other second producer at scale before 2031; none is on a published schedule.
evidence.confirm_by: No confirmation needed; dated public source

evidence.claim: P7. United States import duties on wire, cold heads, logic, memory and graphics rest on Section 232 and Section 301 measures with no expiry after the Supreme Court ended emergency-power tariffs on 20 February 2026: 10 percent combined for the European Union, United Kingdom, Taiwan and Canada, 12.5 percent for Japan, South Korea, China and Brazil from 24 July 2026. A 50 percent tariff on the copper content of worked copper has applied since 1 August 2025. Magnet-grade niobium-titanium wire in a copper matrix sits outside the copper annex and outside the control lists.
evidence.source: Federal Register (5 Aug 2025); Supreme Court (20 Feb 2026); EY (Jul 2026); foreign trade, macroeconomic, contrarian lenses
evidence.changes_if: A trade deal that removes Section 232 measures, or a reclassification of the wire into the copper annex. The wire classification is AI-suggested; Sourcing confirms the declared code.
evidence.confirm_by: No confirmation needed; dated public source

evidence.claim: P8. The Section 232 investigation into medical equipment opened on 2 September 2025 names MRI machines in scope, and no proclamation had followed by 11 October 2026. The tools for restricting trade in finished scanners exist and are court-proof; whether they are used, and at what rate, is open.

The European Union has excluded Chinese-origin medical devices from public tenders at or above 5 million euros since 30 June 2025 with no expiry, and China barred European Union firms from imported-device procurement above 45 million yuan from 6 July 2025 while exempting products made in China. The China plant keeps Asian market access that a United States-built scanner loses, and is not a backup for Europe.

Cyber duties with dates inside the horizon are law: United States device cyber law since March 2023 with final guidance February 2026; the European Union Cyber Resilience Act reporting from 11 September 2026 and full application 11 December 2027 for bought-in electronics; the United States Coast Guard port cyber plan deadline 16 July 2027; Japan mandatory reporting from 1 October 2026; China's amended law from 1 January 2026.

evidence.claim: P11. An encrypted manufacturer takes five weeks or longer to restart on the 2025 record, which is past the 30-day tolerance line. Programmable logic was the most reported counterfeit part class in 2025 at more than 15 percent of reports. Cargo theft hit 2,646 confirmed incidents in 2025 with electronics the most targeted type.

evidence.claim: P12. The United States manufacturing workforce had a median age of 43.9 in 2025, about a quarter is 55 or older, and the cohort turning 65 between 2025 and 2027 is the largest on record. Union density in South Carolina (2.8 percent) and Wisconsin (6.4 percent) sits far below the national rate, so slow attrition of untracked trades is the likelier labour failure, not a strike. Japan and Germany, home to the sole cold-head and wire sources, are shrinking their working-age populations through the 2030s.
evidence.source: BLS tables 18b and 11b (2025); BLS union tables (2025, 2026); Statistics Bureau of Japan (2024); KfW (1 Jul 2025); labor lens
evidence.changes_if: The contrarian notes welders' median age (39.3) is below the all-worker median, so the "retirement cliff" is a property of one roster, not of the trade. The OEM's roster age is AI-suggested; Human resources confirms.

evidence.claim: P13. The East Coast longshore master contract covering the export port runs to 30 September 2030 with automation protections; the last stoppage (October 2024) lasted three days. The port's hurricane closures are two to three days on its own logs; the closure class that breaches 30 days is a blocked channel (Baltimore, 11 weeks in 2024). The port has spare berth after suspending its newest terminal on 1 August 2026.

evidence.claim: P14. Grid recovery after an inland storm in South Carolina ran about ten days after Helene (2024). The reliability body rates the Carolinas grid elevated from 2027 with winter-morning risk and the Midcontinent grid high from winter 2028 on coal retirements and contracted data-centre load. The Pee Dee basin behind the magnet plant had three 100-year rainfall events in 2015 to 2018, and the design rainfall that continuity plans use will be rewritten no earlier than September 2027.
